applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a stackable award rather than a standalone one: you only reach it by first securing and accepting an Otago international entrance scholarship such as the Vice-Chancellor's or Global Scholarship, and the invitation to apply arrives in eVision afterwards. Plan your money around what it actually covers - first-year residential college accommodation plus $7,000 of tuition in each of years two and three - because food, insurance, flights and any rent above the standard college room rate stay on your bill. If you would rather live in a private flat in first year, the scholarship pays you nothing that year, so confirm you want college life before you rely on the figure.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international school leavers who want a residential-college first year and can hold a 7.0 (A-) GPA to keep the tuition component in years two and three.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure an Otago Offer of Place and accept your earlier international scholarship offer first - the invitation only follows that acceptance
Monitor eVision after your offer lands, because the invitation window to complete the scholarship questions is only two weeks
Decide early whether you will live in an Otago residential college in year one, since declining it forfeits the year-one payment entirely
Plan for a 7.0 (A-) GPA in first year, as years two and three tuition support depends on satisfactory academic performance
Confirm you are not sponsored by your home government or the New Zealand Government, which disqualifies you outright
common_rejection_risks: Letting the two-week post-invitation window lapse in eVision
Assuming the ~$35,000 covers everything, when it is accommodation plus two years of tuition and nothing else
Letting the first-year GPA fall below 7.0 and losing the years two and three tuition payments
Enrolling in a diploma or certificate, which are not degree programmes and are ineligible
Being sponsored by a home or New Zealand Government scheme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, health insurance, flights to and from New Zealand, and any accommodation cost above the standard University college room rate; no payment at all is made in year one if the recipient does not live in a University residential college.
document_audit: There is no separate document upload - everything is submitted through eVision, so a missed eVision task is a missed application
The earlier scholarship offer and the admission offer must both be accepted before the invitation is triggered
Keep evidence of secondary study completed overseas, since eligibility hinges on having studied outside New Zealand
alerts: Deferral is not possible for this scholarship - if you cannot start by the enrolment date in your Offer of Place the award lapses and you are reassessed
Semester 2 starters receive only half the accommodation funding in year one, with the remainder released the following February
If your residency status changes from international to domestic, the University may terminate the scholarship and require repayment in part or in full
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme application and scholarship consideration both run inside eVision: apply, accept your entrance scholarship, then complete the invited scholarship questions within two weeks.

official.status_note: Published on Victoria University of Wellington's scholarships site as a current award for international students entering Master's or Postgraduate Diploma study.

benefits: NZ$10,000 credited towards tuition fees only, applied directly to tuition fees upfront so students pay the reduced amount

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic award, so your programme application doubles as your scholarship application and the money shows up as an upfront tuition credit in your Offer of Place if you qualify. The two traps to plan around are duration and eligibility drift: the credit covers only one year of a Master's that typically runs 18 months to two years, and ordinary moves like taking advanced standing or arriving as a Study Abroad or Exchange student quietly switch it off. Keep your fee status international until the credit lands, because a change to domestic status withdraws the scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded international students starting a full-time on-campus coursework or thesis Master's (or 120-point Postgraduate Diploma) with no advanced standing and no government sponsorship.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your programme's point value - only 120, 180 or 240-point Master's degrees and 120-point Postgraduate Diplomas qualify
Apply early enough to hold an unconditional or conditional Offer of Place before your intake begins
Avoid credit transfer, advanced standing or recognition of prior learning from any earlier qualification
Confirm you are not sponsored by your home government or the New Zealand Government before relying on the award
Keep your fee status international until the credit is applied, as a change to domestic status withdraws the scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Entering as a Study Abroad, Exchange or Twinning student, or as a returning student outside the EAP or Bachelor's pathway
Holding advanced standing or recognition of prior learning from a previous qualification
Being an Australian or New Zealand citizen, permanent resident or resident visa holder, or holding a diplomatic visa with domestic status
Applying for a programme outside the qualifying point values, such as a 60- or 90-point qualification
Fee status changing from international to domestic before the scholarship is credited
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition for the second year of multi-year Master's programmes, plus living costs, insurance and flights - the credit is tuition-only and runs for a single year.
document_audit: There are no scholarship-specific documents; the only paperwork is your programme application and the Offer of Place, so errors are admission errors
The scholarship does not appear on your academic transcript, so keep the Offer of Place letter as your proof of award
Deferral requests need approval and are limited to another intake within the same calendar year - a later year forfeits the award
alerts: Only one scholarship is formally awarded per student even if you receive multiple Offers of Place; it is formalised when you enrol in first-year courses
Withdrawing after the formal award can require repayment of some or all of the value at the University's discretion
The award cannot be deferred to a later year, only to another intake within the same calendar year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No separate submission: apply for the programme, receive the Offer of Place confirming scholarship eligibility, then enrol in first-year courses for the award to be formalised.
